reference: Contract cases use Bash's documented `type -t` and `help` builtins and static ionice help text documented in config/bash-loadables.list and loadables/ionice.c. The expected type tag is `builtin`; help assertions check documented summary, synopsis and option descriptions. No ionice operation was run to derive an expectation. Deferred operations are intended for comparison with util-linux ionice(1) plus a deterministic ioprio_get/ioprio_set mock that never forwards calls to the kernel.
coverage: Bash recognizes ionice as a builtin with PATH empty.
Bash help exposes the documented ionice summary, synopsis, classes, levels and ignore-fail option.
Deferred: own-process and explicit-PID query output, including all scheduling class formats.
Deferred: class aliases, default set values, explicit priority bounds and class-specific data handling.
Deferred: malformed and overflowing arguments are rejected before any ioprio syscall.
Deferred: repeated PID processing, syscall failures and -t behavior.
Deferred: command form, option terminator, child output and exit-status propagation.
exclusions: No ionice operation is invoked: even queries call the loadable, and setters or command form can alter process I/O scheduling. All operation scenarios require a future disposable VM or an equivalent deterministic syscall mock.
Metadata checks are contract coverage only; they do not count as operation coverage or GNU ionice parity.

cases.purpose: Check Bash reports the loadable as a builtin without invoking ionice. The `builtin` type tag is the documented result for a shell builtin.
Check help metadata remains available and contains the loadable's documented summary, invocation synopsis and option descriptions, without calling the ionice operation.
cases.script:
help_text=$(help ionice)
[[ $help_text == *'Get or set the I/O scheduling class and priority of a process.'* ]]
[[ $help_text == *'ionice [-c CLASS] [-n LEVEL] -p PID...'* ]]
[[ $help_text == *'-c CLASS  none|0, realtime|rt|1, best-effort|be|2, idle|3'* ]]
[[ $help_text == *'-n LEVEL  0 (highest) .. 7 (lowest); default 4'* ]]
[[ $help_text == *'-t        ignore set failures'* ]]
printf '%s\n' 'documented help present'

cases.purpose: Compare own-process and explicit-PID queries for none, realtime, best-effort and idle classes, including priority formatting and get failures.
cases.reason: Requires a future disposable VM or deterministic ioprio_get mock supplying packed class/priority values and controlled errors to both the candidate and util-linux ionice(1). No process query was run here.

cases.purpose: Compare numeric and named class aliases, default best-effort class/priority, explicit levels 0 and 7, and the effective data for none and idle classes.
cases.reason: Set operations can mutate process scheduling and realtime class changes may require privilege. A future disposable VM or syscall mock must intercept ioprio_set for candidate and GNU ionice(1), record the requested class/data, and never forward the call to the host kernel.

cases.purpose: Check missing option operands, unknown classes, priorities outside 0..7, malformed/overflowing PIDs and excessive PID lists, while confirming rejected requests make no syscall.
cases.reason: Although these inputs should fail before mutation, they still invoke the loadable. A future syscall-mocked disposable fixture must compare util-linux ionice(1) status/diagnostics and verify the mock recorded no ioprio_get/ioprio_set calls.

cases.purpose: Check processing of multiple explicit PIDs when one target fails, accumulated status, and -t/--ignore behavior for failed sets.
cases.reason: Requires deterministic per-PID success and failure injection for both implementations. A future disposable VM or syscall mock must use only fixture PIDs, record call order and errors, and ensure no mock call reaches the kernel.

cases.purpose: Check command form applies the requested policy to a child, honors -- before command arguments, preserves child output and propagates its exit status; also check set failure versus -t continuation.
cases.reason: Command form forks and attempts to change the child's I/O priority before exec. A future disposable VM or syscall-mocked runner must intercept ioprio_set for candidate and util-linux ionice(1), execute only a small relative fixture command, and verify child output/status without any real kernel priority change.
